title: Reference
description:
A shortcut to other content, placed in a container's library tree.

A `Reference` is a pointer wearing a name — it holds no content, only a link. Its purpose is to
let one piece of content appear in more than one place without being duplicated: a monster
defined in a compendium can be listed under the chapter it ambushes the party in, and a map can
be filed under two locations at once.

It differs from an inline link in `Page/content` by being a first-class library item: it sits
in the tree with its own name, position and `parentId`, so it shows up when browsing rather
than only when reading.

- Note: The link is a soft one. Nothing keeps a reference and its target in step, so
  `linkedObject()` returns `nil` once the target is gone.

- SeeAlso: `Group`, `Page`, `Module`

id.description:
The unique identifier for this reference.

A UUID string automatically generated when the reference is created. This serves as the
primary key in the Realm database.

name.description:
The display name of the reference.

Shown in the library in place of the target's own name, so a link can be labelled for the
context it appears in.

## Examples
- `"Klarg (Bugbear Boss)"`

slug.description:
A URL-friendly identifier for the reference.

## Examples
- `"klarg-bugbear-boss"`

reference.description:
The app URL of the content this reference points at.

## Examples
- `"/monster/bugbear"`
- `"/map/cragmaw-hideout"`
- `"/page/goblin-ambush"`

- SeeAlso: `linkURL`, `linkedObject()`

parentId.description:
The identifier of the `Group` containing this reference in the library tree.

Empty for a reference at the top level of its container.

rank.description:
The manual sort position among its siblings.

Lower values sort first.
